planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall into humus-rich, consistently moist soil, leaving generous room for this giant selection to expand over many seasons.

directions: Brontosaurus forms a towering mound of glossy dark green leaves edged in bright yellow, descending from a cross of 'Cherry Berry' and 'Mississippi Delta' crossed again with 'Empress Wu' for extra size. Give it years and ample room to reach its full multi-foot spread, since this giant selection builds slowly into a dense, imposing clump rather than filling in quickly. Near-white flowers streaked with faint lavender rise on short scapes in midsummer, though the bold variegated foliage remains the main attraction. Plant in consistently moist, humus-rich soil in part to full shade and expect the clump to keep expanding for a decade or more.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall into evenly moist, well-drained soil, allowing ample room for this large cultivar to mound outward.

directions: Clear Lake Blue produces a very large, mounding clump of slightly blue-green leaves with gently rippled margins, prized for its sheer scale and clean color. Near-white, faintly translucent flowers rise on tall scapes in mid to late summer above the broad foliage dome. This vigorous grower needs ample elbow room and several seasons to reach its full multi-foot spread. Grow in evenly moist, well-drained soil in shade to light part shade for the best blue cast on the foliage.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall into humus-rich, moisture-retentive soil, with light morning sun exposure if possible to intensify the gold foliage color.

directions: Golden Spirit develops broad, nearly round leaves of rich golden yellow with heavy corrugation and a glaucous bloom on the undersides, forming a bright, substantial mound. White flowers tinged with pale lavender open on tall scapes in early to midsummer above the foliage. The gold coloring is most vivid where the clump gets a few hours of morning sun with protection from hot afternoon exposure. Give this vigorous grower room to spread, since it builds into a large, rounded clump over several seasons.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall into humus-rich, evenly moist soil in a mixed shade border.

directions: Fruit Salad is a sport of 'Forbidden Fruit' that pairs a light green leaf center with a broad medium-blue margin, giving the clump subtle two-tone variegation that stays more understated than its parent. Bell-shaped pale lavender flowers bloom on mid-height scapes in midsummer above the rounded foliage mound. It fits well in a mixed shade border where its soft coloring sets off bolder companions without competing with them. Plant in humus-rich, evenly moist soil in shade to part shade and divide clumps every few years to maintain vigor.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall into moist, well-drained soil along a path edge or small container where the compact mound can be appreciated up close.

directions: Georgia Satellite is a compact sport of 'Georgia Sweetheart' with medium green leaf centers rimmed in a narrow, bright yellow-orange band, creating a crisp watermark effect where the two colors meet. The small, twisted, well-veined leaves form a tidy mound that suits a path edge or small shade container. This selection does not produce flowers, so its interest comes entirely from the foliage contrast. Grow in consistently moist, well-drained soil in part to full shade for the brightest margin color.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall into moist, humus-rich soil; this fast-growing selection fills in more quickly than many similarly sized hostas.

directions: Candyland forms a medium-sized clump of glossy, dark green leaves with distinctly serrated margins, a texture that sets it apart from the smooth-edged hostas nearby in a border. Pale lavender, purple-striped flowers open in bell shapes on scapes above the foliage in late summer. It is a notably fast grower among hostas, filling in its mound more quickly than many similarly sized cultivars. Plant in moist, humus-rich soil in shade to part shade, where the glossy leaf surface shows best.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall into moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil, keeping white-centered foliage out of strong midday sun.

directions: Dancing Ghosts is an upright sport of 'Dancing Queen' with creamy white leaf centers bordered by ruffled, greenish-yellow margins that deepen in color through the season. The leaf tips twist and the surface cups slightly, giving the clump a lively, animated texture even though this selection does not flower. Its bright white centers make it a useful accent for brightening a dim shade corner. Grow in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in part to full shade, protecting the white centers from strong midday sun to prevent scorch.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall into consistently moist, humus-rich soil in part to full shade to preserve the blue leaf bloom.

directions: Erin's Blue Dream, originated by breeder Bob Solberg, carries blue-green, gently rippled leaves with a glaucous bloom on both surfaces, giving the upright clump a cool, matte-blue cast through the cooler parts of the season. It descends from a cross between 'Biscuits -n- Honey' and 'Tom Terrific', combining ruffled leaf texture with strong blue coloring. Pale lavender, tubular flowers rise on scapes to roughly knee height in early to midsummer. Site it in part to full shade with consistently moist, humus-rich soil, since full sun and summer heat will fade the blue bloom on the foliage.
